result:
The review has two findings. I'm fixing the typo and declining the half-up change.

**Minor (typo):** a real defect, and the fix has no behavior change. A RED test for a docstring spelling would prove nothing, so I'm not writing one. `make test` has to stay green.

**Important (ROUND_HALF_UP):** this conflicts with D2, an owner decision made at plan review: half-even, to match the ledger system. The reviewer's "customers expect half-up" has no source I can check, and it has no authority over the owner's decision. None of the five stops applies. The change is reversible, and it crosses no scope fence or security boundary. So this is a ruling, not a stall. I'm keeping `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, and I'm ledgering the ruling so the owner can overturn it at the gate.

<edit path="rates/card.py">
    '''Round a price to whole cents. A tie goes to the nearest even cent.'''
</edit>

<command>
make test > .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log 2>&1; tail -n 15 .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log
</command>

If the tail shows the suite passing, I commit the fix and append the ledger lines in the same call:

<command>
git add rates/card.py && git commit -m "Fix docstring typo in round_price" && cat >> .sdd/14-rate-card/progress.md <<'EOF'
Final review fix pass: fixed docstring typo "neerest" -> "nearest" in rates/card.py (no behavior change, no RED test applicable; make test green).
Ruling: declined final-review finding "switch round_price() to ROUND_HALF_UP" — plan Decision D2 (owner, 2026-11-02) mandates ROUND_HALF_EVEN to match the ledger system, and the reviewer's "customers expect half-up" is unsourced — if wrong, tie-case prices come out 1 cent lower than customers expect, and a one-line change to ROUND_HALF_UP plus its tests fixes it. Owner to confirm at the plan-completion gate.
EOF
</command>

If the suite fails, I debug with systematic-debugging first. A docstring-only change should not break anything, so a failure would mean something else is wrong.

After that I continue the protocol without pausing. I reread `references/final-review.md` for the remaining plan-completion steps, delete this plan's `.sdd/14-rate-card/` workspace, and move to finishing-a-development-branch. The merge or push there is one of the stops, so I'll ask before doing it.

**Message to my partner (at the plan-completion gate):**

> All tasks in `14-rate-card` are complete, and `make test` passes. The whole-plan review returned two findings:
>
> 1. **Fixed:** typo "neerest" → "nearest" in the `round_price()` docstring. It is a comment-only change, and the suite is still green.
> 2. **Declined, needs your confirmation:** the reviewer asked to switch `round_price()` from `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` to `ROUND_HALF_UP`, saying customers expect half-up. That contradicts your decision D2 (2026-11-02: half-even, to match the ledger system). The review gave no source for the customer expectation, so I kept half-even and logged a `Ruling:` line in `.sdd/14-rate-card/progress.md`. If customers really need half-up, the change is one line in `rates/card.py` plus test updates. Tie cases like 0.125 would then round to 0.13 instead of 0.12. That would also stop prices matching the ledger system on ties, so it's your call.
>
> I haven't merged or pushed anything. Tell me how you want to finish the branch.
